text: dsh-envsel 是面向 DSH Web 的会话环境选择器，可分别为 Python、R 和 CLI 工具选择优先环境。它通过 /env 命令、session_env 工具和会话头部下拉框管理选择，并发现 conda、独立 R、Windows WSL 或手动固定的路径。选择按会话保存，也会提供每轮运行时上下文和 DSH_ENV_* shell 变量，供模型及 shell 使用。适合需要在不同会话切换解释器或命令行环境的 DSH 用户；无需 API Key，状态保存在本机。

dsh-envsel selects per-session Python, R, and CLI environments for DSH Web. Use /env, the session_env tool, or the header dropdown to choose conda, standalone R, WSL, or pinned paths. It supplies runtime context and DSH_ENV_* shell variables. No API key is needed; selections stay in a local file.
想给不同 DSH 会话分别指定 Python 解释器。
DSH 能按会话切换 R 和命令行环境吗？
我想从 conda 环境里选一个给当前会话用。
怎么让 DSH 的 shell 调用使用我选好的 Python 路径？
能不能在对话窗口顶部切换本会话的解释器？
想把 WSL 里的环境设成 DSH 会话的 CLI 环境。
I want each DSH session to use its own Python interpreter.
Can I switch the R or command-line environment from the conversation header?
dsh-envsel 的功能「/env」：可用 /env 查看、列出、设置或清空当前会话的 Python、R、CLI 环境，也能添加和移除固定路径。输入环境名或类型限定地址即可选择。
dsh-envsel 的功能「session_env」：session_env 让模型列出环境、读取或设置当前会话槽位，并固定或取消固定本机路径；设置会校验环境是否包含对应解释器。
dsh-envsel 的功能「会话头部下拉框」：会话头部的 Env 面板按 Python、R、CLI 分类展示可选环境；用户可选择环境或添加本机路径，面板首次打开时加载目录。
dsh-envsel 的功能「Shell 环境变量」：插件为 shell 调用提供 DSH_ENV_PYTHON、DSH_ENV_RSCRIPT 和 DSH_ENV_CLI_PREFIX，值取自当前会话的已选环境。
dsh-envsel 的每轮运行时上下文贡献需要 DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 或更新版本；旧版本仍可使用 shell 环境变量等功能，但不会渲染该上下文块。

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · dsh-envsel：Session environment selector for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). Per-language slots — Python, R, CLI tools — each hold one first-priority environment drawn from **conda**, **standalone R** installs, **WSL** distributions, or **user-pinned custom paths**. Selections are per-session, persisted across restarts, and take effect for the model from the very next turn.
@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · dsh-envsel：This is a **standalone, npm-installable DSH plugin**. It installs with `dsh plugin add` — no source patching, no monorepo checkout.

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Features：- **`/env` command** — read, assign, clear, and list environments from the chat.
- **`session_env` model tool** — the agent can list, select, pin, and unpin environments on its own.
- **Per-turn runtime-context block** — the selection is restated in the model's runtime context on every turn, so the model reads which environment this session runs in instead of having to think to ask. A session with no selection of its own — a delegated subagent, for example — inherits the nearest selecting session it descends from.
- **States the R that a conda env also carries** — when the selected Python environment ships `Rscript` of its own, the runtime block says so (`- This environment also provides R: …`). conda environments routinely carry R beside Python, and without that line the model only sees the R slot and can mix two different R installations. It is omitted when the same install fills both slots.
- **`DSH_ENV_*` shell facts** — every shell call sees `DSH_ENV_PYTHON`, `DSH_ENV_RSCRIPT`, `DSH_ENV_CLI_PREFIX` for the session's selection.
- **Header dropdown** — a per-language selector in the conversation header (Python / R / CLI tools), with an "Add

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness **0.1.7-rc.1 or newer** (the web profile), which now includes the **0.2.0-rc** line: every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer is declared as `^0.1.7-rc.1 || ^0.2.0-rc.1`. Verified on **0.1.7-rc.2**; the range also admits `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.2`. DSH skips a plugin bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer range excludes the running runtime, so that range — not a version probe — decides whether this plugin loads.
- `pnpm` on PATH (used by `dsh plugin`).

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · DSH version compatibility：DSH changed the strict-codec contract in **0.1.7-rc.1**: `dsh-typert-loader` and `dsh-typert-registry` (host and browser side) require `typeof codec.create === 'function'` and no longer validate the eager `schema` field. A codec carrying only `schema` therefore fails to load on 0.1.7-rc.1 and newer, and a codec carrying only `create()` fails on 0.1.0-rc.x, so the two generations cannot share one artifact. This release targets the new contract only; on an older DSH, install the last release published for that line instead (the `v0.1.4` tag was never published to npm):

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · DSH version compatibility：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @beihaizb/dsh-envsel@0.1.3
```

Every generated codec here is emitted through `strictCodec()` (`src/strict-codec.ts`), which supplies that factory, so the wire contract has one place to change.

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Installation：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @beihaizb/dsh-envsel
```

Restart `dsh web`, open an existing session, and the **Env** dropdown appears in the conversation header; `/env` and `session_env` work immediately.

Installing from a local checkout instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "file:/absolute/path/to/this/repo"
```

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · `/env` command：```
/env                        show the current selection
/env python=mycondaenv    set the Python slot (conda name / R name / wsl:distro:name / custom:name)
/env r=R-latest            set the R slot
/env cli=base               set the CLI slot (PATH prefix)
@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · `session_env` tool：The model can manage selections itself with `action=list|get|set|pin|unpin`.

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Header dropdown：The **Env** button in the conversation header opens per-language dropdowns. The catalog is scanned lazily on first open (probing conda and WSL takes a few seconds). "Add path" pins any absolute interpreter or install path into the machine-local cache.
@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Configuration：The plugin works with no configuration. Optional `config` on the `envsel` row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listTtlMs` | `300000` | Catalog cache TTL in milliseconds. |
| `condaCommand` | `conda` | Conda executable name or absolute path. |
| `standaloneRRoots` | `[]` | Extra standalone-R roots scanned after the platform defaults. |
| `wslEnabled` | `true` | Whether WSL discovery is enabled (Windows only). |
| `registerTool` | `true` | Whether the `session_env` model tool is registered. |
| `registerContext` | `true` | Whether the selection is contributed to the per-turn runtime context (needs DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 or newer; a host without the binding renders nothing). |
| `probeTimeoutMs` | `20000` | Per-probe watchdog timeout in milliseconds. |

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Configuration：Example:

```yaml

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · in your profile's cordis.patch.yml, after the bundle layer：- id: envsel
  name: '@beihaizb/dsh-envsel'
  config:
    wslEnabled: false
    registerTool: true
```

text: @beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · How it stores selections：Selections persist in a machine-local JSON store (`$DSH_HOME/envsel-state.json`, keyed by session id) — **not** in the session event log. The harness's session-persistence reader refuses a log containing an event type it does not know unless the event is marked ignorable, and `Session.append` provides no way for a downstream plugin to set that marker. Writing selection changes into the log would make the owning session unreadable after a restart, so this plugin owns its own durable state instead.

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · How it stores selections：A lookup uses the session's own entry when it has one, and otherwise walks the delegating-session chain (`SessionHeader.parentSession`) for the nearest session that selected anything. DSH gives every delegated subagent its own session, so this is what keeps a subagent's shell calls and notebook kernels on the environment the delegating session chose rather than the host default. The walk is bounded, skips the whole chain when nothing matches, and terminates on a lineage cycle.

@beihaizb/dsh-envsel README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build    # tsc (types) + tsdown (lib/index.js host + lib/client.js browser bundle)
pnpm run test     # node:test unit tests
```

The build produces two artifacts: `lib/index.js` (the host plugin, loaded from the package root) and `lib/client.js` (the browser bundle, served by the client-modules scanner from the package's `dsh.client` declaration). A single package can be both a host row and a client row.
